proposal.thesis: Micron just delivered one of the cleanest beat-and-raise prints in the AI-supplier cohort: Q3 FY26 revenue of $41.5B (guided next quarter to $50B, +20% QoQ) with gross margin at 85% and guided to ~86%, an EPS beat of 24% ($25.11 vs $20.20 est). The company disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements worth roughly $100B of minimum contracted revenue, including $18B of customer cash deposits to secure HBM supply that is sold out through 2026 with demand outstripping supply by 50-67%. Despite the print and today's +12% reaction, the stock still trades at just 5.5-6.8x forward earnings versus a 30.6x semiconductor sector median, and the balance sheet is a fortress (net cash ~$23.75B, debt/equity 0.06, TTM FCF $26.2B). The setup is a post-earnings-drift trade, not a chase into an unresolved binary: the print already happened and the thesis is that the market has not yet re-rated the multiple to reflect the newly-disclosed, quantified demand visibility.
catalysts: Q3 FY26 earnings beat + Q4 FY26 guide to $50B revenue / ~$31 EPS / ~86% gross margin, reported 2026-07-22
16 Strategic Customer Agreements ~$100B minimum contracted revenue incl. $18B cash deposits, disclosed 2026-07-22
HBM capacity sold out through 2026, demand 50-67% above supply per management commentary
Next earnings print ~2026-09-22 (outside this swing's 45-day horizon)
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive (SPY 748 vs 694 200-DMA, score 4/5) with cooling Fed funds but a rising 10Y (4.60%) and reaccelerating CPI (3.46% YoY) - a real headwind for richly-multipled growth, but MU trades at 5.5-6.8x forward earnings (82% discount to the 30.6x semis median) so it is one of the least rate-sensitive ways to own the AI buildout. Momentum-factor is flagged 'unwind' at the ETF level (MTUM -8.3% off highs) even though our own 3-month leader cohort (which includes MU) reads 'healthy' - sizing already reflects the code's automatic 0.5x haircut.
proposal.risk_map: Primary risk is that today's post-earnings pop is the whole move (sell-the-news chase) rather than the start of a re-rating drift; memory is a historically boom-bust cyclical and the market may simply not extend the multiple regardless of the backlog. A DRAM/NAND pricing air-pocket, a hyperscaler pausing HBM orders, or a broader semi-sector de-rating (the chips_crack_20 stress scenario) would hit this position hard given its 8.4% ATR. Sized at roughly half the normal risk budget given the momentum-factor unwind flag, and the stop is set at 1.4x ATR (11.8%) to survive ordinary post-earnings volatility, without an options expected-move cross-check since MU was outside this run's deep-research focus set.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Sell-side is already bullish (Strong Buy, KeyBanc $1,750 PT, ~$1,490 mean target) yet MU still trades at just 5.5-6.8x forward earnings, an ~82% discount to the 30.6x semiconductor sector median. MY VIEW: the market is still pricing this as a garden-variety boom-bust memory cycle rather than a structurally-scarce, multi-year HBM supercycle. MECHANISM: today's print disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements worth ~$100B of MINIMUM CONTRACTED revenue, including $18B of customer CASH DEPOSITS to secure supply - a quantified, non-slideware signal of demand visibility that historical memory cycles never had, and which the stock's cyclical-discount multiple has not yet re-rated to reflect even after today's pop. RESOLUTION: the FY26 Q4 print (~2026-09-22, guided $50B revenue / ~$31 EPS / ~86% gross margin) and any HBM4/customer-agreement follow-on news over the next 30-45 days will show whether the backlog converts as guided; if it does, the multiple re-rates further even without new news.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: Q4 FY26 report or any pre-announcement showing gross margin guidance walked back below ~80% (vs the ~86% just guided) or bookings/backlog not converting from the disclosed $100B Strategic Customer Agreements would kill this thesis.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close back below $880 (below both the pre-earnings resistance-turned-support zone and roughly the 50-DMA) on above-average volume would show the breakout has failed and the gap is being reversed.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If MU has not sustained a close above $1,050 (meaningful follow-through beyond today's gap) within 30 trading days of entry, the drift thesis is not confirming and the position should be reduced or rotated.

proposal.thesis: DDOG's own stated watchlist trigger ('stabilized base above $250 post-downgrade digestion') fired today: shares reclaimed and held above $250 on a fresh, dated catalyst (JMP Securities raised its target to $311 from $225, citing infra-software strength over apps-software). Fundamentals support the re-rate: revenue +45.9% yoy (Q ended 2026-03-31), $1.06B TTM FCF, net cash balance sheet, and the book's own validated volume read (no_supply_pullback) confirms healthy accumulation rather than a low-conviction pop. Institutional ownership_flow reads institutions_buying_price_rising - real sponsorship behind the move, not just retail chase. Sized and timed AROUND the 8/6 earnings print (14-day horizon), not through it, given elevated options event premium.
catalysts: JMP Securities price target raise to $311 from $225, 2026-07-22, citing infra-software over apps-software strength
8/6/2026 Q2 print (outside this trade's 14-day horizon by design)
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive (SPY above both 50/200-DMA, credit spreads compressing, VIX soft) though momentum_health reads softening at the factor level (MTUM/SPMO drawing down vs SPY) - favors a name with an idiosyncratic, dated catalyst over generic momentum chase, which is what this is.
proposal.risk_map: Insider signal is notable_discretionary_selling: $388.8M of open-market sells over 120 days, 16 distinct non-plan officer/director sells, zero buys - real distribution, sized for with a smaller-than-full-budget position rather than skipped outright since price/volume/fundamentals show no matching deterioration. Options market prices real pre-earnings event risk (ATM IV 73.5%, expected move +/-9.7%, put skew 6.2pp over calls) - mitigated by a 14-day AROUND-earnings horizon rather than holding through 8/6. Stock is only 8.6% below its 52-week high, so a failed reclaim (close back below $250 on volume) invalidates fast and cheaply given the stop is only 10% away.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Street already rates DDOG strong_buy (46 analysts, mean recommendation 1.49) with a pre-catalyst mean target near $265, i.e. priced for continued execution but not for acceleration. MY VIEW: the market has not yet caught up to today's JMP target hike to $311 (+38% from $225), which specifically calls out infrastructure software outperforming applications software in the AI cycle. MECHANISM: sell-side models built off last quarter's 45.9% yoy growth print understate how much of that growth is AI-workload observability attach rather than legacy infra monitoring - the differential question this book's own stack_cards flags for DDOG - so if the 8/6 print shows accelerating net-new ARR / RPO from AI-native customers, consensus estimates get revised toward JMP's number rather than away from it. RESOLUTION: the 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings print (product revenue growth, net new ARR, RPO growth) and whether other sell-side desks follow JMP's re-rate in the weeks after.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: The 8/6 print (or any pre-announcement) shows decelerating net-new ARR or RPO growth versus the prior quarter, or a guide cut - would confirm the re-rate thesis was premature.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close back below $250 on above-average volume - a round-trip failure of today's reclaim, undoing the exact trigger this trade was built on.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If DDOG has not made a fresh high above $270 by 2026-08-04 (two trading days before the 8/6 print), exit or cut before the print regardless of thesis - this is an AROUND-earnings trade, not a binary bet, and the horizon exists to force that decision.

proposal.thesis: IBKR beat Q2 2026 estimates on EPS ($0.69 vs $0.65) and revenue (~$1.88B vs ~$1.80B), with client equity up 40% YoY to $930B and a 77% pretax margin for a 7th straight quarter above 70%. The stock closed the session +2.99% to $94.42, above both its 50- and 200-DMA, 3.5% off its 52-week high, with a pocket-pivot volume day corroborating genuine participation rather than a low-volume drift. Unlike GS's faded premarket spike or CB/NOC's weak or structurally broken reactions among today's other earnings movers, IBKR's move is orderly, in-trend, and under-owned by the momentum/AI-stack complex currently unwinding. Next earnings is not until 2026-10-20, well outside this swing's horizon, so this is a clean post-print continuation trade with no binary event risk in the window.
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings beat reported 2026-07-21 (EPS $0.69 vs $0.65 est; revenue ~$1.88B vs ~$1.80B est; record $930B client equity, +40% YoY)
Expected sell-side EPS/target revisions over the next 1-2 weeks following the beat
Next earnings 2026-10-20 — outside this swing window, no binary risk
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive (SPY above its 200-DMA, 64.5% of universe above its own 200-DMA, A/D 1.58) with rising 10Y/2Y yields that are a direct tailwind to a broker's net interest income. Momentum_health flags a factor unwind (MTUM -8% off highs) that specifically threatens AI-stack momentum leadership; IBKR's `financials` demand driver sits outside that complex, which is the intended diversifying response to an unwind rather than another momentum-dependent AI name.
proposal.risk_map: Primary risk: today's reaction could still fade like GS's premarket spike did (GS closed only +2.9% after a +7.7% premarket pop) — if IBKR gives back this gain over the next 1-2 sessions and closes back under the post-earnings gap low, the continuation thesis is wrong and I exit at the stated invalidating_structure level rather than average down or hope. Secondary risk: IBKR's revenue is levered to trading volume and net interest income — a sharp, unexpected dovish Fed pivot or a volatility collapse would remove both tailwinds simultaneously; the rising-yield backdrop right now argues the opposite, but that backdrop can reverse fast.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Sell-side rates IBKR 'buy' (mean 1.75, 12 analysts) with a $105.41 mean target implying only ~12% upside even after today's beat, and coverage framed the print as 'good but largely priced in' given the stock's flat-to-down 1-month drift into the quarter. MY VIEW: the market is underweighting how structural the margin story now is — a 77% pretax margin for a seventh straight quarter above 70%, alongside record $930B client equity, is durable operating leverage, not a one-quarter beat, and a muted (not euphoric) reaction leaves room for the multiple to re-rate as estimates catch up. MECHANISM: sell-side EPS models for IBKR have consistently undershot net-interest-income and trading-activity assumptions in this rising-real-yield regime (10Y up to 4.60%, 2Y up to 4.21%) — this is IBKR's fourth consecutive beat, and each one has come from the same underestimated drivers. RESOLUTION: the next 1-2 weeks of post-print analyst estimate revisions, and whether price holds/extends above today's gap rather than fading it, will show whether the model-lag mispricing is real.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: A guidance signal of decelerating DARTs/client-equity growth, a reversal in the 70%+ pretax margin trend, or a subsequent quarter showing net interest income rolling over would kill this thesis.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close back below the 50-DMA on rising volume, or a close back under approximately $90 (below today's post-earnings gap low), would show the reaction has failed rather than continued.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If IBKR has not sustained a close above $100 within 25 trading days of entry, exit and rotate the capital — a post-earnings continuation trade needs to show follow-through within weeks, not months.
